summary: Frontend-only re-test of Teologia Viva PWA (iteration 2). Auth page UI renders correctly and all protected routes (/, /academia, /biblia, /comunidade, /eventos, /anotacoes, /perfil) correctly redirect unauthenticated users to /auth. HOWEVER, every signup attempt returns HTTP 429 'over_email_send_rate_limit' directly from Supabase and login on a pre-existing unconfirmed account still returns 400 'email_not_confirmed'. This is conclusive evidence that the Supabase project STILL has 'Confirm email' ENABLED (fix #1 from iteration 1 was NOT actually applied / saved). With email confirmation on, signup triggers a confirmation email and the project-level rate limit blocks it → no session is ever returned. Every authenticated feature (devocional, academia, curso, aula, biblia, comunidade, eventos, anotacoes, perfil, tutor IA, rate limit) remains UNTESTABLE end-to-end.

ui_bugs.issue: Confirm email is STILL enabled. Direct curl POST /auth/v1/signup returns {code:429, error_code:'over_email_send_rate_limit', msg:'email rate limit exceeded'} → only possible when Supabase is trying to send a confirmation email. When Confirm email is OFF, signup returns an access_token/session and no email is attempted.

When Supabase returns 429 the toast shows the raw supabase-js error 'Failed to execute \'json\' on \'Response\': body stream already read' instead of a PT-BR message like 'Muitas tentativas — tente novamente em alguns minutos'. Add a branch in submit() for err.status===429 or err.message.includes('rate limit') → toast.error('Muitas tentativas em pouco tempo. Aguarde alguns minutos.').

integration_issues.issue: Signup fails 429 so navigation to / never happens. Account is not even created (rate-limited before insert).

qatest1777585550@gmail.com still returns 400 email_not_confirmed → confirms Confirm-email was not disabled. test+1777585472@teologia.test returns 400 invalid_credentials (that account was never actually created — signup had failed).

action_items: CRITICAL BLOCKER: In Supabase dashboard → Authentication → Providers → Email → DISABLE 'Confirm email' (toggle off) and click SAVE. Verify by re-running: curl -X POST $SUPABASE_URL/auth/v1/signup -H 'apikey: $ANON' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"verify@qa.test","password":"TestPass123"}' → response MUST contain access_token (not 429). As long as that curl returns 429 or no session, the PWA cannot be tested end-to-end.
Wait for the project rate limit to cool down (may take up to 1 hour on free-tier SMTP) before re-running this test so the first confirming-signup can succeed.

Nice-to-have: in /app/frontend/src/pages/Auth.jsx submit(), add: `if (err?.status === 429 || /rate limit/i.test(err?.message || '')) toast.error('Muitas tentativas. Aguarde alguns minutos e tente novamente.');` — currently the PT-BR UX regresses to a raw internal JS error string for rate-limited signups.

Once the blocker is cleared, re-run iteration 3 to validate: signup → trial badge → Inicio devocional → Academia → Curso → Aula → Tutor IA drawer → Biblia (book/chapter picker, verse drawer, btn-explicar-ia) → Comunidade (vou-orar, novo-pedido) → Eventos (GPS prompt) → Anotacoes CRUD → Perfil (logout) → bottom nav.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.jsx signUp() correctly short-circuits with {needsEmailConfirmation:true} when data.session is null, so the PT-BR 'Conta criada! Confirme seu email para entrar.' toast path would work — but the 429 path never reaches that branch because supabase-js throws before returning data. Good defensive coding though.
AuthContext.jsx catch{} around the profiles upsert silently swallows errors; once the profile table is verified with real columns, consider logging a console.warn so schema drift is detectable.

Auth.jsx does not handle err.status explicitly; relies on err.message string matching. Fine for now but prone to i18n/locale regressions from Supabase. Consider switching on err.code/err.status when supabase-js v2 surfaces them.
/app/frontend/.env keeps the Supabase URL/anon key — OK, expected for client bundle. No backend to test.
Protected route guard works: all 7 tested protected paths redirect to /auth when unauthenticated — good.

success_rate.frontend: Auth page UI + Protected routing verified (≈15%). All 14 authenticated feature tests BLOCKED (0% of 14).

rca of the issue: Root cause: Supabase Auth setting 'Confirm email' is still ENABLED for project wuwmjovqdahlpfkncydg. Evidence: (1) Direct curl POST /auth/v1/signup → HTTP 429 {code:429, error_code:'over_email_send_rate_limit'} — this error code is only emitted when Supabase attempts to send a confirmation email (email sender throttled). If confirmation were off, signup would simply return a user+session with no email. (2) Login on a previously-created-but-unconfirmed account qatest1777585550@gmail.com returns HTTP 400 {code:'email_not_confirmed'} — same account would succeed if confirmation had since been disabled (Supabase auto-validates unconfirmed users on next login when the flag is turned off). Mitigation: toggle Authentication → Providers → Email → 'Confirm email' OFF in Supabase dashboard and hit Save. Then wait ~5 min for the SMTP rate limit window to clear. Reproduction: open /auth → tab 'Criar conta' → fill nome/email (unique)/senha → click 'Começar trial de 7 dias' → URL stays on /auth and an error toast appears. Secondary/cosmetic bug: the toast displays a raw supabase-js internal error string instead of a PT-BR rate-limit message — fix in /app/frontend/src/pages/Auth.jsx submit() catch branch.
